whatThePageStates: The page is a catalogue of the AWS Managed Rules baseline rule groups for AWS WAF. It has three H2 sections, one per rule group: Core rule set (CRS) (AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet, WCU 700), Admin protection (AWSManagedRulesAdminProtectionRuleSet, WCU 100) and Known bad inputs (AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet, WCU 200). Each section gives the VendorName, Name and WCU cost, a paragraph on what the group protects against, a boilerplate note that the content describes the most recent static version, and one two-column table (Rule name | Description and label) listing the rules the group contains. There are 35 rule rows in total (22 + 1 + 12). The page asserts only presence: every rule listed exists in its group, with a default rule action and a label. It never says any rule or group is unavailable, and it carries no Region, account, plan or resource-type support matrix.

features.collapse: The 35 table rows are individual rules, not rule groups. They sit under three H2 rule-group sections and collapse to three distinct managed rule groups: AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (22 rows: NoUserAgent_HEADER through CrossSiteScripting_URIPATH), AWSManagedRulesAdminProtectionRuleSet (1 row: AdminProtection_URIPATH) and AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet (12 rows: JavaDeserializationRCE_HEADER through ReactJSRCE_BODY). The label prefix in each row confirms the parent group (core-rule-set, admin-protection, known-bad-inputs). 22+1+12=35 rows, 3 groups.
features.statuses: 35 present, 0 not-supported, 0 partial; 22+1+12=35. There is no status column of any kind. Presence in the table is the only signal, so every row reads as an implicit Yes. Not-supported is entirely ABSENT from this page - no No, no 'isn't available', no exclusion note - so no negative count can be derived. Each row does carry a default 'Rule action' (all 35 read 'Rule action: Block'), but that is the rule's behaviour, not a support status, and must not be mapped onto Yes/No.
features.scope: One weak scope: version. Each section states 'This documentation covers the most recent static version release of this managed rule group' and points to the changelog and DescribeManagedRuleGroup for other versions, so the 35 rules describe the latest static version only. Two rows further note that log match details are not populated for version 2.0 of the CRS group. There is no Region, partition, account-type, pricing-plan or scan-method dimension anywhere on the page.
features.reasoning: managedRuleGroup is the catalogue AWS publishes about itself, and this page is one chapter of that catalogue (the baseline chapter, alongside the bot, IP reputation and use-case-specific chapters). The unit a coverage measure should carry is the rule group, because that is what a customer adds to a web ACL and what has a VendorName, Name and WCU. The rule rows are the internal composition of each group, one level finer than the axis, which is exactly the row-versus-target case.

shouldNotExtract: The console-experience banner at the top. The repeated four-line Note block in each section (most-recent-static-version disclaimer, the 'we do not publish everything so bad actors cannot circumvent the rules' paragraph, the Support Center link) - three identical copies, not three data points. The WCU numbers (700, 100, 200) - these are capacity costs, i.e. quota arithmetic, not coverage. The 'Rule action: Block' and 'Label: awswaf:managed:aws:...' fragments inside each Description cell - behaviour and metric identifiers, not statuses. The body-size-limit prose repeated in every _BODY rule ('8 KB for Application Load Balancer and AWS AppSync; 16 KB default, up to 64 KB for CloudFront, API Gateway, Amazon Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway') - these are inspection quotas, and the service names in them are examples inside a limit sentence, not a support matrix. The header-limit prose ('first 8 KB of headers or first 200 headers'). CVE identifiers (CVE-2022-22963, CVE-2022-22965, CVE-2021-44228, CVE-2021-45046, CVE-2021-45105, CVE-2025-55182) and example attack patterns - illustrations, not axis values. The two table header rows repeated three times and their '| --- | --- |' separators. The whole 'See also' section, which is the optional AI-coding-assistant / Agent Toolkit skills boilerplate.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no partition, and makes no availability statement of any geographic kind. Any per-Region number attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing usable. AWS WAF is the subject, not an enumerated value, and the only other AWS service names on the page (Application Load Balancer, AWS AppSync, CloudFront, API Gateway, Amazon Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, CloudWatch) appear inside body-size-limit sentences or metric prose - they are not a protected-service support list, and the list is not even self-consistent (the ReactJSRCE_BODY row names seven of those eight, omitting Bedrock AgentCore Gateway). RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. The phrase 'the body size limit for the protection pack (web ACL) and resource type' gestures at resource types but the page enumerates none as supported or unsupported. What the page does give is a catalogue dimension only: 3 baseline managed rule groups containing 35 named rules.
trap: The single most likely misparse: reading 35 as the number of managed rule groups. The page has three tables that a row-counting parser will merge into one 35-row list, and every row looks like a named, self-contained protection. It is 35 rules inside 3 rule groups. Runners-up: (1) treating 'Rule action: Block' as a status column and reporting 35 Yes / 0 No, or worse, inventing a No bucket - there is no negative claim anywhere on this page, so any not-supported count is invented; (2) harvesting the 8 AWS service names from the repeated body-size-limit sentence as a service or resourceType support matrix, which would also inherit the ReactJSRCE_BODY inconsistency and produce 7 in one row and 8 in the others; (3) counting the three identical Note blocks, the three header rows, or the WCU values as data; (4) mistaking WCU 700/100/200 for a coverage figure; (5) forgetting that the page is scoped to the most recent static version of each group, so the 35 is a point-in-time count, not a stable one; (6) pulling the 'See also' Agent Toolkit bullet in as page content.
